rounds.fact: Juno offered free dial-up internet paid for entirely by advertising, and later merged with rival NetZero to survive the end of the free-ISP era.
Groupon grew explosively fast off its daily-deal email format and turned down a reported $6 billion buyout offer from Google in 2010, a decision still debated years later.
Xbox.com launched alongside Microsoft's first console in 2001, marking the company's first serious entry into a gaming hardware market long dominated by Sony and Nintendo.
Shutterfly built its business on printing physical photo books from digital pictures, a bridge business between film photography and today's all-digital photo storage.
CNN.com's early design crammed dozens of headlines onto one dense page, a layout style that dominated news sites for years before cleaner, story-focused redesigns took over.
